issues: Uses dropna() which silently drops None/NaN values from the input; the problem says to count occurrences, so None values should likely be counted as well (though this is a minor edge case).

Converting via pandas DataFrame is unnecessary overhead; iterating the list directly is simpler and avoids potential dtype coercion issues (e.g., integers being converted to floats when NaN is present, which would change the Counter keys).
If the input list is empty, pd.DataFrame(d) produces a DataFrame with no columns, so all Counters will be empty — this works but relies on pandas behavior.
